plan.summary: This 4-week block is the opening build phase of a 12-week off-camp boxing plan. With only one 45-minute S&C session each week and sparring taking priority, the work stays focused on explosive lower-body power, simple full-body strength, and a small amount of trunk and neck work. Week 1 establishes a baseline squat training max for future loading, and the main build starts in Week 2.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic strength and general power with simple, repeatable lifts that do not interfere with sparring.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main lifts and keep power work sharp while holding total fatigue in check.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with lower volume and express faster, sharper power for boxing-specific output.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on quietly and cleanly. Reset between reps and focus on fast takeoff and controlled landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if box setup is awkward. Jump for height and stick the landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use bodyweight only and keep each rep crisp.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hard set with clean form. Stop if depth or bracing breaks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: This session sets your baseline for future percentage work. Warm up in small jumps, then complete one hard top set of 3-5 reps and log the load and reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels more stable on the shoulders and upper back.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if barbell squatting is not yet comfortable. Make the top set technically hard, not sloppy.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean top set of 3-5 reps.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Drive elbows back and pause briefly at the top. Keep the torso glued to the pad and control the lowering.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench for support and avoid twisting.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a neutral or close grip and keep the chest tall.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Only roll as far as you can keep ribs down and lower back flat. Move slowly out, then pull back under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no ab wheel is available.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rollouts are too difficult. Keep the trunk doing the work.

exercises.name: Plate Neck Flexion and Extension
exercises.notes: Use very light load and smooth tempo. Stop well before strain and keep the range controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Harness Neck Extension and Flexion
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a very light load and strict control.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Keep every rep springy and clean. Stop a set early if jump height drops or landings get noisy.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Jump for height and reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Trap Bar Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only a light load and move fast.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Brace hard, reach full depth you can control, and drive up fast. Leave 1-2 good reps in reserve on the final set.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it keeps position cleaner and easier to coach.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if front rack and depth are comfortable.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track bar weight and reps from the best-looking work set.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Bench Press

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
